brief.headline: SK Hynix ships HBM4E samples, extends lead; DRAM/NAND pricing spike continues; Samsung HBM4 qual progressing
brief.summary: SK Hynix announced 12-layer HBM4E sample shipments to customers today (June 18), hitting record highs intraday (+5.91% to ₩2.67M) and reinforcing its 58% Q1 HBM market share lead. Memory pricing remains structurally tight: TrendForce forecasts Q2 DRAM contracts +58-63% QoQ and NAND +70-75% QoQ as HBM/server reallocation starves commodity supply. Hyperscaler capex exceeded $112B in Q1 alone, with AWS guiding ~$200B for 2026 and TSMC CoWoS capacity ramping to 115-140K wpm by year-end. Samsung delivered HBM4E samples May 29 and reportedly passed Nvidia HBM4 SiP tests; both are competing for 2027 Rubin Ultra design wins.
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix vs flat/short Samsung Electronics. Hynix's HBM dominance (58% share Q1, monopoly on Blackwell HBM3E, HBM4E delivery on schedule) is widening the earnings delta: Q2 OPM est. +578% YoY for Hynix vs +1,756% for Samsung (but Samsung mix diluted by MX/DX/SDC). Foreign inflows concentrated exclusively in Hynix (₩3.1T net buy over 4 days ending June 16); market-cap gap now smallest ever at 2.5x vs historical 5-7x. Samsung's HBM4 qual progress is real but late; Hynix's pure-play memory exposure commands higher multiple in AI infrastructure upcycle. Near-term catalyst asymmetry favors Hynix into H2.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-upcycle tightness, transitioning HBM3E→HBM4 with pricing power intact
memory_cycle.notes: Q1 2026 DRAM contracts +90-95% QoQ, Q2 +58-63% QoQ; NAND Q1 +55-60%, Q2 +70-75%. HBM/DDR5 server reallocation creating 3:1 wafer conversion ratio squeeze on commodity DRAM. HBM3E remains 66% of HBM shipments in 2026 per LS Securities; HBM4 ramps H2 2026 for Rubin (launch H2 2026). Capacity relief unlikely until late 2027; CSPs signing LTAs at elevated prices. DDR5 RDIMM and eSSD from data centers forming dual pillars alongside HBM.

brief.hbm_pulse: SK Hynix HBM4E (12-hi, 48GB, 16Gbps, +20% power efficiency vs HBM4) sample delivery confirms schedule discipline and extends technology lead. Samsung shipped HBM4E samples May 29, triggering direct head-to-head qual race for Nvidia Rubin Ultra (2027). Counterpoint data: Hynix 58% Q1 share, Samsung/Micron each 21%. Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery, accelerating transition cadence. HBM3E-to-HBM4 inflection steepening in H2; 12-layer HBM4 mass production target early 2026 met by Hynix, Samsung close behind. MR-MUF vs hybrid bonding remains process fork: Hynix maximizing proven MR-MUF; Samsung exploring hybrid bonding for 7th-gen HBM4E. TSMC CoWoS bottleneck easing (120-140K wpm 2026E) but utilization remains high.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers; shares +5.91% to ₩2.67M record high
news_pulse.implication: On-schedule HBM4E delivery reinforces technology leadership and locks customer engagement for 2027 Rubin Ultra. 48GB capacity, 16Gbps/pin, +17% heat resistance vs HBM4. Qualification race with Samsung (delivered May 29) now in motion.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI hits 9,000 intraday; Samsung +2.31% to ₩354.5K, SK Hynix +5.91% to ₩2.67M
news_pulse.implication: Memory rally extending; foreign flows heavily tilted to Hynix (₩3.1T net buy over 4 days). Market-cap gap Samsung/Hynix narrowest ever at 2.5x. Momentum favors pure-play memory exposure.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q2 2026 DRAM contracts +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ; supply remains tight
news_pulse.implication: Pricing power intact despite sequential moderation from Q1's +90-95% DRAM spike. HBM/server reallocation sustaining undersupply across all segments. CSPs signing LTAs to guarantee allocation; no capacity relief until late 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler Q1 2026 capex hits $112B combined; AWS targeting ~$200B for full year
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented infrastructure spend directly drives HBM/DDR5/eSSD demand. AWS +19% YoY, Azure +39%, Google Cloud +48% in Q1. AI workload monetization accelerating; memory supply remains binding constraint through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity ramping to 115-140K wpm by end-2026, 170K wpm in 2027
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing but utilization remains high. Nvidia locked >60% of 2025-26 capacity. CoWoS-L adoption for Blackwell/Rubin enabling 12-16 HBM4 stack integration. HBM supply constraint shifting from packaging to DRAM fab capacity.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix eyeing Honam region for first back-end packaging plants
news_pulse.implication: Domestic capacity expansion driven by HBM packaging demand. Samsung reviewing Gwangju/Saemangeum; Hynix considering Gwangju/Muan. Signals multi-year commitment to advanced packaging infrastructure in Korea.

news_pulse.headline: Gartner forecasts DRAM prices +125% YoY 2026, NAND +234% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Annual price inflation projections reflect compounding quarterly increases and structural shift away from commodity memory. Procurement teams front-loading orders; spot volatility forcing hourly pricing models.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung reports Q2 OPM est. ₩8.68T (+1,756% YoY); SK Hynix ₩6.25T (+578% YoY)
news_pulse.implication: Both posting steep earnings growth in AI memory supercycle, but Samsung's diversified structure (MX/DX/SDC) diluting upside vs Hynix pure-play leverage. Brokerages raising TPs: Nomura ₩590K Samsung, ₩5M Hynix; SK Securities ₩610K/₩4M.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI broke 9,000 intraday June 18 for first time, up from 8,000 close May 26 (16 trading days). Implied vol likely elevated on Hynix given parabolic move (+50% YTD) and record concentration of foreign positioning. No specific options data in payload, but single-stock futures/options flow would favor Hynix calls into H2 Rubin ramp and Q2 earnings (early July). Watch for gamma squeeze risk if ₩2.7M level holds; resistance at ₩3M psychological. Samsung comparatively range-bound; call spreads may offer better risk/reward than outright longs.
